questions.q: The equation $(\cos p-1) x^2+\cos p x+\sin p=0$ in the variable $x$, has real roots. Then, $p$ can take any value in the interval
questions.solution:

questions.q: The least value of $a$, for which the function $\frac{4}{\sin x}+\frac{1}{1-\sin x}=a$ has atleast one solution in the interval $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, is
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{4}{\sin x}+\frac{1}{1-\sin x}=a\Rightarrow \quad 4(1-\sin x)+\sin x=a \sin x(1-\sin x)\Rightarrow \quad 4-4 \sin x+\sin x=a \sin x-a \sin ^2 x\Rightarrow \quad a \sin ^2 x-(3+a) \sin x+4=0$  ....(i)
It is a quadratic equation in $\sin x$, so $D \geq 0\begin{array}{cr}\Rightarrow & (3+a)^2-4 \times 4 a \geq 0 \\ \Rightarrow & 9+a^2+6 a-16 a \geq 0 \\ \Rightarrow & a^2-10 a+9 \geq 0 \\ \Rightarrow & (a-1)(a-9) \geq 0\end{array}\Rightarrow \quad a \geq 9$ or $a \leq-9$
Now, at a = 9, Eq. (i) becomes
$9 \sin ^2 x-12 \sin x+4=0\Rightarrow \quad(3 \sin x-2)^2=0\Rightarrow \quad \sin x=\frac{2}{3} \lt 0 \Rightarrow x \in\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$
Hence, least value of $a$ is 9 .

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the equation $x^2+p x+q=0$ and $x^2+q x+p=0$ have a common root then $p+q+1$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given equations are
$x^2+p x+q=0$  ...(i)
$x^2+q x+p=0$  ...(ii)
Let $\alpha$ be the common root, then
$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha^2+p \alpha+q=0 \text { and } \alpha^2+q \alpha+p=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\alpha^2}{p^2-q^2}=\frac{\alpha}{q-p}=\frac{1}{q-p}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \alpha^2=\frac{(p-q)(p+q)}{-(p-q)}=-(p+q) \ldots$...(iii)
and $\quad \alpha=\frac{q-p}{q-p}=1$  ...(iv)
$\therefore$ From Eq. (iii)
$\begin{aligned} & & \alpha^2 & =-p+q \\ \Rightarrow & & (1)^2 & =-(p+q) \quad[\text { from Eq. (iv) }] \\ \Rightarrow & & p+q & =-1 \Rightarrow p+q+1=0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\tan A$ and $\tan B$ are the roots of the equation $x^2-a x+b=0$, then the value of $\sin ^2(A+B)$ is
questions.solution:
Since, $\tan A$ and $\tan B$ are the roots of the equation $x^2-a x+b=0$. Therefore,
$\tan A+\tan B=a$ and $\tan A \tan B=b$
Now, $\quad \tan (A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A \tan B}=\frac{a}{1-b}$
Now, $\quad \sin ^2(A+B)=\frac{1}{2}[1-\cos 2(A+B)]\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \sin ^2(A+B)=\frac{1}{2}\left\{1-\frac{1-\tan ^2(A+B)}{1+\tan ^2(A+B)}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin ^2(A+B)=\frac{1}{2}\left\{1-\frac{1-\frac{a^2}{(1-b)^2}}{1+\frac{a^2}{(1-b)^2}}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin ^2(A+B)=\frac{1}{2}\left\{\frac{2 a^2}{a^2+(1-b)^2}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin ^2(A+B)=\frac{a^2}{a^2+(1-b)^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $2 a+3 b+6 c=0$, then atleast one root of the equation $a x^2+b x+c=0$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
Consider the function
$f(x)=\frac{a x^3}{3}+\frac{b x^2}{2}+c x+d$
We have, $\quad f(0)=d$
and $\quad f(1)=\frac{a}{3}+\frac{b}{2}+c+d\begin{aligned} & =\frac{2 a+3 b+6 c}{6}+d \\ & =\frac{0}{6}+d \quad[\because 2 a+3 b+6 c=0]\end{aligned}$
Therefore, 0 and 1 are roots of the polynomial $f(x)$. Hence, according to Rolle's theorem, there exists atleast one root of the polynomial $f^{\prime}(x)=a x^2+b x+c$ lying between 0 and 1.

questions.q: If $a=\cos \frac{2 \pi}{7}+i \sin \frac{2 \pi}{7}$, then the quadratic equation whose roots are $\alpha=a+a^2+a^4$ and $\beta=a^3+a^5+a^6$, is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } a=\cos \frac{2 \pi}{7}+i \cdot \sin \frac{2 \pi}{7} \\ & \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad a^7 & =\cos 2 \pi+i \sin 2 \pi \\ & =1 \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$
Also, $\alpha=a+a^2+a^4, \beta=a^3+a^5+a^6$ then the sum of roots, $\begin{aligned} S & =\alpha+\beta=a+a^2+a^3+a^4+a^5+a^6 \\ \Rightarrow \quad S & =\frac{a\left(1-a^6\right)}{1-a}=\frac{a-a^7}{1-a} \\ & =\frac{a-1}{1-a}=-1 \quad\left[\because a^7=1\right] \end{aligned}$
Product of the roots, $\begin{aligned} & P=\alpha \beta=\left(a+a^2+a^4\right)\left(a^3+a^5+a^6\right) \\ & =a^4+a^5+1+a^6+1+a^2+1+a+a^3\left[\because a^7=1\right] \\ & =3+\left(a+a^2+a^3+a^4+a^5+a^6\right)=3-1=2 \end{aligned}$
Hence, the required quadratic equation is $x^2+x+2=0$

and $g(x)=-x^2-2 c x+b^2$
